title: Back Pain
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} presents with localized lower back pain, fever, chills, malaise, and point tenderness over the affected vertebrae. Vertebral osteomyelitis is a bacterial infection of the vertebral body — most commonly S. aureus. Risk factors: IV drug use, recent bacteremia, indwelling catheters, DM, immunocompromised. Diagnosis: MRI spine with contrast (gold standard — high sensitivity). Plain X-ray may be normal early (need 30-50% bone loss to see). Blood cultures x2 (positive in 50%). If blood cultures negative → CT-guided or open biopsy for culture. ESR and CRP elevated. Treatment: IV antibiotics (empiric: vancomycin + ceftriaxone or cefepime — cover MRSA and gram-negatives) x 6 weeks minimum, tailored to culture results. Surgical debridement if abscess, neurologic deficit, spinal instability, or failure of medical therapy.
